question: A shopkeeper has 2220 kg of rice. A part of which he sells at a 20% profit and the rest at a 12% profit. He gains 18% on the whole. The quantity ( in kg ) sold at a 12% profit is:
solution:
Given:

A shopkeeper has 2220 kg of rice. A part of which he sells at a 20% profit and the rest at a 12% profit. He gains 18% on the whole. 

Calculation:

Using mixture and alligation,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48235270e53e65caf4863e83ede5aa05868ecc5828eebba57b977dcc7d2448ef.png] 

So, the ratio of the quantity of rice that is sold at 20% profit to the quantity of rice that is sold at 12% = 3 : 1

Now, the quantity of rice that is sold at 12% profit = 2220 × 1/(3 + 1) = 555 kg

**∴ The quantity sold at a 12% profit is 555 kg.**
